Backend: 7 strict pass + 1 xfailed (per-IP rate limit ineffective behind k8s ingress — works on localhost). Loretta video-question reply correctly says 'not supported / future release'.

minor.issue: Per-IP rate limit (6/IP/5min) not effective through Kubernetes ingress / public preview URL — 7 consecutive calls all returned 200. _check_report_rate_limit uses request.client.host, which behind the ingress resolves to an ingress IP (or varies per hop), defeating the bucket key. Verified the limiter DOES work correctly on internal http://127.0.0.1:8001 (7th call=429). Fix: read X-Forwarded-For (right-most untrusted hop) and fall back to request.client.host. Also keep in mind a single-IP NAT will share one bucket — could need user_agent + ip combo.

action_items: Fix rate-limit IP source in /app/backend/routers/help_chat.py::_check_report_rate_limit — read X-Forwarded-For first hop, fall back to request.client.host. Without this the 6/5min cap is ineffective in cloud deploy.
critical_code_review_comments: _REPORT_BUCKET in /app/backend/routers/help_chat.py grows unbounded — every distinct IP gets a permanent entry. Add periodic GC or use a TTL cache (cachetools.TTLCache) keyed on IP. Memory is small (~200 bytes/entry) but unbounded over years.

routers/help_chat.py imports `notify_webhook.notify_team` inside the request handler (line 378). Hot-path import is cheap (Python caches) but moving to module-top would be cleaner and one less try/except surface area.

build_capabilities_payload() in /app/backend/routers/platform_capabilities.py is called synchronously inside async route handler — fine because it's pure-Python and tiny (~6KB output), but the 'cached at the edge for 60s' comment is aspirational only — the route ALWAYS rebuilds the dict and the global middleware overrides Cache-Control to no-store anyway. Either drop the misleading header set or wire a real ETag / lru_cache.

SYSTEM_PROMPT_BASE concatenation in help_chat.py (~3KB) happens per request. Acceptable today, but if capabilities payload grows past ~6KB the per-request prompt build cost will matter — consider lru_cache(maxsize=1, ttl=60s) on the assembled prompt skeleton.

HelpReportIssueIn.conversation accepts up to N turns with each text capped at 4000 chars — no aggregate cap. A malicious client could post a 100-turn array (each 4000 chars) = ~400KB body. FastAPI/Starlette has a default request size limit but consider an explicit `max_items` on the conversation list (e.g., 20).

rca of the issue: Rate limit not firing through public preview URL: _check_report_rate_limit keys its bucket on `request.client.host`. In the k8s ingress topology, that field is populated from the immediate socket peer — the ingress pod — not the real client. Each request can also be served from a different ingress pod with a different IP, so the bucket key changes between calls. Localhost direct hits (same 127.0.0.1) trigger 429 on the 7th call as designed. Mitigation: parse X-Forwarded-For (left-most non-private hop) and fall back to request.client.host.
